title: No Verified Record Can Defend Vietnam’s Dog Meat Trade
excerpt: Available records establish no pet-theft case, seizure, court verdict, or trade incident here. Claims need proof. Public health still demands quarantine and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No police seizure, court verdict, intercepted shipment, or named Vietnamese health alert appears in this report. That absence blocks honest claims about cyanide bait, stolen family dogs, or so-called dog farms. It does not make those claims true—or make the trade safe. Evidence must come before outrage, and accountability must follow evidence.

Myths need records, not slogans

“Tradition” cannot prove lawful sourcing. “Farm-raised dogs” cannot prove quarantine, vaccination, ownership, transport compliance, or humane handling. But no verified case record appears here to establish that stolen pets supply the trade. Responsible reporting must not turn an unverified allegation into a fact.

Biosecurity still demands hard safeguards

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See WHO rabies guidance.

Household rabies exposure and commercial animal transport are separate biosecurity problems. Neither supports invented causal links. Both demand inspection, quarantine enforcement, transparent records, and protection for Vietnamese families and companion animals.

Turn verified demand into reform

SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030. That campaign demand differs from any official public-health target. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, and require authorities, police, courts, and health agencies to publish the records needed for honest reform.

Seek urgent medical assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis, including vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms develop, rabies is virtually 100% fatal.

Vietnamese families deserve safe communities, transparent animal transport, real quarantine enforcement, and protection for companion animals. Household exposure and commercial supply chains are separate risks; both require accountable institutions and published records.
